escalation.obstacle: Construct a GADGET_4: a 4-COLOURABLE finite unit-distance graph G with non-adjacent marks p,q at distance != 1 such that G + pq is not 4-colourable. By Theorem B the third required colour exclusion cannot come from a common neighbourhood, which is the whole difficulty.
escalation.definitions: A unit-distance graph is a finite graph with an injection into R^2 such that uv is an edge iff |u-v| = 1. Proper k-colouring: c(u) != c(v) on every edge. A pair is forced equal at k if G is k-colourable and G plus the edge pq is not; the added edge is a combinatorial disequality constraint and, for a non-adjacent pair, never a unit edge. Diamond: K_4 minus an edge, vertices a,b,t1,t2, edges ab, at1, at2, bt1, bt2, |t1-t2| = sqrt3. Coordinates in Q(sqrt3, sqrt11) or Q(sqrt3, sqrt5, sqrt11).
escalation.hypotheses: Exact real-algebraic coordinates; complete finite graph; k = 4 with G 4-colourable (this hypothesis is the one that failed for the 553-vertex graph, which is 5-chromatic).
escalation.attempted_approaches: Palette excluders via common neighbours (Theorem B: at most 2 vertices, so only 2 colours excludable); clique-sum gluing (Theorem A: cannot raise chi); common-unit-neighbour stacking (the operation is an involution); exhaustive forced-pair census on the spindle family; a 553-vertex no-forcing certificate at k>=5 (34 witnesses, complete); and now a specified cross-unit seed S1 with a prepared bounded test.
